name: X-Linked Lymphoproliferative Disease Type 1

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Genetic Diagnostic Criteria for XLP1

criteria.description: Identification of pathogenic mutation in SH2D1A gene
Severe or fatal Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) infection or hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis (HLH) triggered by EBV
Evidence of immune dysregulation such as hypogammaglobulinemia or defective cytotoxic T-cell/NK cell function
Family history of male relatives with similar immunodeficiency or early death from EBV-related complications

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of pathogenic SH2D1A mutation plus clinical evidence of severe EBV infection or HLH
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing is essential for definitive diagnosis; clinical presentation may vary.

pathognomonic.notes: Often presents as fulminant infectious mononucleosis or HLH

common.notes: Reduced immunoglobulin levels leading to recurrent infections
Enlarged lymph nodes during EBV infection or HLH episodes
Enlarged liver and spleen common in HLH and EBV infection
Due to immune dysregulation and hypogammaglobulinemia

occasional.notes: Including seizures or encephalopathy during HLH
Due to immune dysregulation or infections
May occur during HLH or immune activation

laboratory: Low or absent SAP protein expression
Elevated ferritin and triglycerides during HLH episodes
imaging: Hepatosplenomegaly on abdominal ultrasound or CT
Pulmonary infiltrates on chest X-ray or CT
genetic: Pathogenic mutations in SH2D1A gene on X chromosome
X-linked inheritance confirmed by family studies
other: Defective NK cell and cytotoxic T-cell function assays

distinguishingFeatures: HLH can be familial or secondary; XLP1 specifically linked to SH2D1A mutations and EBV susceptibility
XLP1 predominantly affects males with X-linked inheritance
CVID presents with hypogammaglobulinemia but lacks severe EBV susceptibility and X-linked inheritance
CVID onset usually later in childhood or adulthood

redFlags: Fulminant or fatal EBV infection in young male
Family history of male relatives with early death from EBV or immune dysregulation
references: Sumegi J, et al. X-linked lymphoproliferative disease: clinical and molecular features. Hematol Oncol Clin North Am. 2015.
Nichols KE, et al. X-linked lymphoproliferative disease due to SAP/SH2D1A deficiency. Immunol Rev. 2011.
